## TL;DR


- **Weave is an engineering-intelligence platform for teams evaluating code output, quality, delivery, and AI spend.** Silk 1 scores the work inside pull requests; Engineering Intelligence and Token Intelligence add review, delivery, usage, and cost context.
- **The key comparison is how a platform measures work.** Counts of commits, PRs, and story points cannot distinguish a routine fix from a complex migration. Weave estimates the expert effort represented by code changes on a common scale.
- DX combines developer experience research with productivity and AI analytics. Jellyfish focuses on engineering investment and AI Impact. LinearB combines analytics with workflow automation. Swarmia provides team-level feedback and AI cost reporting.


Weave publishes this guide. The product descriptions use the first-party sources linked below, reviewed October 16, 2026.


## What is a developer productivity platform?


A developer productivity platform brings engineering data together to help teams understand how work flows, what gets delivered, and where quality or developer experience can improve. The label is an umbrella, not a standardized feature set: products may emphasize delivery analytics, developer-experience research, engineering investment, or code-level intelligence.


This guide compares products that overlap across those jobs; it is not a ranked benchmark. An internal developer portal is a separate category centered on a software catalog, templates, and self-service platform workflows. The term “developer productivity platform” here means analytics and improvement of engineering work, not a developer portal.


## How to evaluate developer productivity platforms


Use the same teams, repositories, and date range when comparing products, then ask:


- **Coverage:** Which GitHub or GitLab organizations and repositories are connected? How are people matched across source control, issue tracking, CI/CD, and AI tools, and what data is missing?
- **Work and output:** Does the platform count commits, PRs, stories, or lines, or does it also assess the scope and complexity of code changes? Can you inspect how a score was produced?
- **Delivery and quality:** Can you review delivery measures alongside review cycles, reverts, incidents, and code churn? DORA metrics are useful, but they describe delivery performance rather than the full value or difficulty of engineering work.
- **Developer experience:** Does the product include team feedback or surveys, and can you interpret those signals alongside system data?
- **AI spend and output:** Is cost provider-billed, usage-derived, configured subscription cost, or an estimate? Is it available per person or only by organization? What attribution evidence is used, and what does the cost denominator mean?


Cost per merged PR, cost per story, and cost per estimated expert hour answer different questions. Compare them over a matching period and cohort. A relationship between AI spend and output is useful for investigation, but does not by itself prove that AI caused a productivity change.


## Weave: engineering intelligence for code output, quality, and AI impact


[Weave](https://weaveos.com/products/engineering-intelligence) is an engineering-intelligence platform that combines code analysis, productivity, and AI intelligence. It gives engineering and finance teams a shared view of output, quality, delivery, and investment. For GitHub and GitLab evaluations, confirm repository access, identity mapping, and which source data is available to your organization.


### Understand the work inside every PR


[Silk 1](https://weaveos.com/products/code-intelligence) reads the full diff and reasons about intent, risk, complexity, and dependencies across files. Output is measured in the effort an expert engineer would need to complete the change, giving teams a common unit across people, repositories, and languages.


Every score includes a plain-language explanation. Team overrides feed organization-aware calibration. Silk 1 reports 3.3× lower average prediction error than its earlier model, with 88% of PR scores within ±1h of an expert estimate.


This is the distinction between counting work items and understanding the work: a short change that affects a large system can be more significant than a long, routine diff.


### Connect AI activity and spending to results


[Token Intelligence](https://weaveos.com/products/token-intelligence) tracks AI adoption, usage, cost, and AI-associated code contributions. Attribution evidence can come from a native tool integration, commit metadata, or a time-series estimate; the method matters when interpreting a result. Cost reporting distinguishes provider billing, modeled usage, subscriptions, and estimates. Costs are available per person when the source supports that detail, while some sources report at organization level.


Compare reported AI costs with AI-associated code output, review effort, code turnover, and delivery. Silk 1 measures merged PR output in estimated expert engineering hours. Weave's[AI ROI methodology](https://weaveos.com/methodology/ai-roi) defines the public cost-per-output-hour calculation and exclusions. This is an observed cost-to-output ratio, not proof that AI caused an outcome. Review the attribution method and source coverage alongside the result, and see the[AI impact measurement framework](https://weaveos.com/blog/ai-impact-measurement-framework-engineering-teams) for a broader measurement approach.


### Find bottlenecks and support financial decisions


Engineering Intelligence measures review depth, rounds before merge, reverts, code churn, incident-to-PR links, and deployment performance. Benchmarks draw on real engineering data from thousands of organizations, segmented by organization size.


Weave also includes R&D capitalization, portfolio views, and[custom dashboards](https://weaveos.com/custom-dashboards) .[Wooly](https://weaveos.com/products/wooly) answers questions about engineering data, and[Weave Checks](https://weaveos.com/checks) runs automated checks on pull requests. Measurement, reporting, and action belong in the same engineering workflow.


## DX: developer experience research and productivity frameworks


[DX](https://getdx.com/) combines developer experience research, delivery analytics, and AI measurement. Its[AI cost management report](https://docs.getdx.com/reports/ai-cost-management/) tracks estimated spend, tokens, credits, and contributor breakdowns, with estimated cost per PR calculated as total estimated cost divided by merged PRs.


DX requires Data Cloud and a supported AI source for this report. Its documentation says merged PRs and estimated cost per PR are unavailable when the report is filtered to a subset of AI tools. Compare the data sources and denominator with Weave's code-based output measure when evaluating AI investment.


Read the[Weave vs DX comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-dx) .


## Jellyfish: engineering investment and AI Impact


[Jellyfish](https://jellyfish.co/) combines engineering investment allocation with operational and AI reporting. Its[AI token cost management product](https://jellyfish.co/platform/jellyfish-ai-impact/ai-token-usage-monitoring/) presents token usage and cost across tools and teams, and describes comparing spend with output and PR throughput.


Financial reporting is also part of Weave. Weave's R&D capitalization analyzes PR output, task associations, and project data, while Silk 1 adds code-level complexity measurement and explainable scores to investment decisions.


Read the[Weave vs Jellyfish comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-jellyfish) .


## LinearB: delivery analytics and workflow automation


[LinearB](https://linearb.io/platform/overview) combines AI usage and impact measurement with code review and workflow automation. Its platform describes AI commit, review-impact, and tool-usage metrics alongside delivery insights, developer-experience surveys, and workflow automations.


Weave adds complexity-aware output, review-depth analysis, code-quality signals, and AI costs to that delivery discussion. Weave Checks provides automated PR checks, while Wooly helps teams investigate their engineering data.


Read the[Weave vs LinearB comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-linearb) .


## Swarmia: team feedback and AI cost reporting


[Swarmia](https://www.swarmia.com/) provides engineering analytics and continuous team feedback. Its[AI ROI view](https://www.swarmia.com/changelog/2026-08-07-ai-roi/) combines an administrator-configured developer cost with the list price of consumed AI tokens, reporting cost per story, merged PR, or line changed.


Weave pairs AI costs with Silk 1's common output scale and engineering quality. Provider billing connections also let teams use actual billed spend where available, with the cost source visible in the report.


Read the[Weave vs Swarmia comparison](https://weaveos.com/compare/weave-vs-swarmia) .

The comparison is not simply whether a platform has an AI dashboard. Check what each product counts as output, how it labels cost and attribution evidence, and whether you can inspect quality and delivery alongside those measures.


## How to choose a developer productivity platform


Start with the question your team needs to answer, then inspect the data behind it.


- **Engineering productivity:** read the output score and explanation for a feature, a bug fix, and a refactor. Check whether the platform recognizes their different scope and complexity.
- **AI investment:** compare spend by person and tool with output and quality over a consistent period; document whether spend is billed or estimated and whether output means PRs, stories, lines, or estimated effort.
- **Delivery improvement:** inspect review cycles, revert rates, deployment performance, and the work behind a bottleneck.
- **Finance and leadership:** use R&D capitalization, portfolio views, and shared dashboards to connect work with investment.

## FAQs


### What makes Weave different from a DORA dashboard?


DORA measures delivery mechanics. Weave also analyzes the code inside every PR, measures output and quality, attributes AI contributions, and connects spending with engineering results.


### Can Weave help with R&D capitalization?


Yes. Weave analyzes PR output, task associations, and project data to identify development work for capitalization. Reports can be broken down by team, repository, or project.


### Does Weave measure individual and team performance?


Yes. Weave reports output and quality at individual and team levels, with a common scoring scale, context for the work, and explanations behind the scores.


### Does Weave support GitHub and GitLab analytics?


Weave connects to GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, and Gerrit. For an evaluation, confirm which organizations and repositories are accessible, how identities are matched, and which PR, review, issue, and delivery signals are available from your connected sources.


### Is a developer productivity platform an internal developer portal?


No. A developer productivity platform analyzes engineering work, delivery, quality, and developer experience. An internal developer portal provides platform-engineering capabilities such as a software catalog, templates, and self-service workflows.


### How should I compare AI spend with engineering output?


Check the cost source, attribution method, reporting granularity, time window, and output denominator. Provider-billed spend, modeled usage, subscription costs, and estimates should be labeled separately. Cost per PR, story, or estimated expert hour are different measures, and none alone establishes that AI caused a change in productivity.


### How does Weave benchmark engineering teams?


Weave uses engineering data from thousands of organizations, with size-based segments and benchmarks for output per engineer, reviews, and delivery performance.
